title: Previous nitrate sample residuals cut test error by 34% at two Gulf river outlets in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether the previous measured nitrate sample improves sequential same-day concentration estimates at two Gulf river outlets. We used USGS release 3.0 and 767 held-out site-dates in water years 2000-2025. Each baseline fit used the preceding 20 years and accounted for flow, season and time. A fixed 60-day decay of the previous sample residual reduced equal-site mean squared log error by 34.18%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was 25.54% to 41.58%. Both sites improved. Later checks with a natural flow spline and a 14-day sample delay retained gains of 33.34% and 31.86%. Raw previous concentration gave no clear gain. Serial correction is an established method; this result adds a chronological benchmark at these two sites. Sparse sampling, related branches, assumed sample availability, model choice and conditional uncertainty limit inference. The result does not establish a physical cause, unsampled-day accuracy or Gulf hypoxia forecast skill. Source extracts, hashes, code, all estimates, a numerical audit and a figure are included.

display.caption: Yearly error reductions and conditional 95% intervals for sequential nitrate estimates. Positive values show lower error than the matched flow, season and time baseline. Spline and delay checks were added after the primary result.

citations.reason: Verified numerical source extracts and prior flow-history benchmark. Observations overlap; no independent data confirmation is claimed.
Established serial-residual correction for river water quality. We add a specific one-sided chronological test, not a new general method.
